metadata.title: Hook patterns — 5 dimensions, 11 modes
metadata.description: HookLens taxonomy: boundary elimination, variable rewards, social traps, sunk cost, and attention hijacking — used when annotating screenshots.

hero.title: A research-informed addiction taxonomy
hero.description: Five core strategies and eleven secondary patterns — shared by Analyze, Vision detect, and Reports. Illustrative labels inspired by CHI / dark-pattern research (e.g. FoSIP-style thinking and Gray-style pattern families), not a formal compliance audit.

patterns.title: Secondary patterns (A1–E2)
patterns.label: Taxonomy
patterns.description: Same IDs as the Analyze picker and AI detector. Grouped under dimensions A–E.

items.title: A1 · Missing stopping cues
items.description: Dimension A — Boundary elimination. Mechanism: cognitive breakpoint deprivation / auto-navigation. Look for: infinite scroll, autoplay / next-episode chrome.

items.title: A2 · Friction removal
items.description: Dimension A — Boundary elimination. Mechanism: low cognitive resistance (Fogg-style triggers). Look for: one-tap buy, swipe-without-confirm loops.

items.title: B1 · Variable ratio rewards
items.description: Dimension B — Uncertainty. Mechanism: Skinner-box intermittent rewards. Look for: pull-to-refresh, loot/unbox, opaque For You rails.

items.title: B2 · Curiosity gaps
items.description: Dimension B — Uncertainty. Mechanism: Information Gap Theory. Look for: vague unread copy, red dots with no preview.

items.title: C1 · Social reciprocity exploitation
items.description: Dimension C — Social traps. Mechanism: reciprocity norms / social pressure. Look for: forced read receipts, streak counters.

items.title: C2 · Fabricated FOMO
items.description: Dimension C — Social traps. Mechanism: loss aversion / bandwagon. Look for: Stories timers, “X also bought” social proof.

items.title: C3 · Quantified approval
items.description: Dimension C — Social traps. Mechanism: extrinsic motivation / self-worth projection. Look for: like leaderboards, huge public counters.

items.title: D1 · Labor & asset accumulation
items.description: Dimension D — Investment. Mechanism: IKEA effect / sunk cost. Look for: check-in trees, non-portable levels and medals.

items.title: D2 · Exit guilt & loss triggers
items.description: Dimension D — Investment. Mechanism: confirmshaming / guilt-tripping. Look for: cancel threats, streak-reset warnings.

items.title: E1 · Artificial urgency
items.description: Dimension E — Attention hijacking. Mechanism: scarcity heuristic. Look for: fake countdown timers, baseless low-stock alerts.

items.title: E2 · Intrusive ping triggers
items.description: Dimension E — Attention hijacking. Mechanism: orienting reflex / habit interruption. Look for: aggressive push chrome for trivial events.

items.question: Is this a formal dark-pattern compliance list?
items.answer: No. It is an illustrative taxonomy for education and screenshot labeling, informed by CHI / regulatory research themes — not a legal checklist.

items.question: Why A1–E2 IDs?
items.answer: Stable codes for Analyze, Vision detection, and Reports. Old labels (infinite/badge/…) map into this scheme automatically.

items.question: Does AI use the same list?
items.answer: Yes. Detect with AI is prompted with this taxonomy and may only return these hookIds.

cta.title: Classify a screenshot
cta.description: Open Analyze, run Detect with AI or pick A1–E2 manually, then generate a report.
